screening_results.reason: Abstract explicitly examines reappraisal and acceptance of negative self-beliefs (meets I2). It investigates the neural basis but does not explicitly state task-based fMRI (I1), inclusion of a healthy control group (I3), or report of task-related activation (I4). No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract. Recommend full-text review to confirm fMRI methods and sample composition.

Task-based fMRI with healthy young adults using distancing (a form of reappraisal) to regulate responses to aversive pictures, and reports task-related brain activation results; meets inclusion criteria I1–I4.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study that included a cognitive emotion regulation task, healthy control group, and task-related activation results (left supramarginal gyrus). The abstract does not specify whether regulation used reappraisal or whether stimuli were pictures, so inclusion is uncertain from abstract alone; include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI randomized placebo-controlled study; participants performed distraction (a form of emotion regulation) while viewing negative pictures; includes trauma-exposed control (healthy) group; reports task-related brain activation. Although the strategy was distraction rather than reappraisal specifically, it meets I2 (emotion regulation) so include for full-text review to confirm details.

Abstract describes a cognitive reappraisal task in healthy younger and older adults and examines neural correlates; however it does not explicitly state use of task-based fMRI or report specific task-related activation in the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm I1 and I4.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult men and women using cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) of negative pictures, and presents task-related brain activation results (vlPFC, amygdala). All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Participants are female adolescents with conduct disorder; the abstract does not report any healthy adult sample, so exclusion E2 applies. The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation and reports task-related brain activation (I1, I2, I4 met). Inclusion criterion I3 (at least one healthy adult group) is not met or not demonstrated in the abstract.

E2 met: study includes adolescent girls (mean age ~14.9) but no healthy adult sample. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performed reappraisal emotion regulation), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I3 (at least one healthy adult group).

Abstract discusses reappraisal and brain–behavior relationships in internalizing psychopathologies but does not explicitly state this is a task-based fMRI study, whether a healthy control group was included, or whether task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to rule out inclusion, so include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study where participants used reappraisal strategies to regulate incidental emotions, includes behavioral and fMRI samples of (presumably) healthy adults, and reports task-related activation in prefrontal and cingulate regions, meeting all inclusion criteria.

E1: Abstract describes a conceptual model/review (no original human data). No evidence in abstract of task-based fMRI, participants performing reappraisal, healthy adult sample, or reported task-related activation (I1-I4 not met).

Excluded (E2): study includes only MDD patients and does not include a healthy adult control group. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; it reports structural cortical thickness/subcortical volumes), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I3 (no healthy adult sample), I4 (no task-related brain activation results).

Excluded (E2): Study uses MRI to predict DBT treatment response in a borderline personality disorder patient sample; abstract provides no evidence of a task-based fMRI reappraisal/emotion-regulation paradigm and does not mention healthy control participants. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1, I2, I3.

Excluded for E2: sample consists only of youth (ages 8–17) and no healthy adult group is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation/variability). Inclusion not met: I3 (no healthy adult sample).

Abstract states the study used functional MRI to investigate reappraisal (an emotion-regulation strategy) in adult patients with ADHD and healthy controls and reports neural correlates, satisfying task-based fMRI, reappraisal task, inclusion of healthy adults, and task-related brain activation reporting. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded (E1): this paper is a meta-analysis of fMRI studies and does not present original human data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a primary task-based fMRI study), I2 (no original participants performing a reappraisal task reported), I3 (no original healthy adult sample), I4 (no original task-related activation results reported; only meta-analytic summaries).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal to downregulate negative emotions in adult women with obesity and healthy female controls, and provides task-related activation results (vmPFC, extrastriate cortex). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I1–I4.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study where healthy adults used reappraisal (and acceptance) to regulate their own emotional responses to idiographic negative self-beliefs and reports task-related brain activation. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

The study used video clips (interpersonal verbal criticism) rather than pictures, so it does not meet the review objective requiring reappraisal of pictures. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Does not address the review objective of reappraisal of emotional responses to pictures: this study examines regulation of recollected autobiographical memories (internal distraction) via attentional focus, not reappraisal of pictures. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 and I4. Inclusion not met or not demonstrated: I2 (reappraisal of pictures not shown; strategy appears attentional deployment of memories), I3 (healthy adult sample not explicitly stated).

Task-based fMRI using a Continuous Emotion Regulation Task where participants watched negative pictures and either maintained or suppressed emotions via reappraisal; includes healthy control group (N=33); reports task-related brain connectivity/activation results. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study assessing emotion processing and reappraisal, includes both alcohol use disorder patients and healthy controls, and examines related brain activity. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Abstract lacks explicit methods/results: it does not clearly state whether this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study, whether participants performed a reappraisal task, or whether a healthy control group and task-related activations are reported. Title implies volitional regulation, but details are insufficient—include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in which participants performed an emotion reappraisal task with attend vs reappraise instructions for emotional and alcohol-related images; includes matched healthy controls and reports neural activation results. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based functional neuroimaging study of emotion processing and regulation including OCD patients, unaffected siblings, and unrelated healthy control participants. This indicates task-based fMRI (I1), an emotion regulation task (I2), and inclusion of healthy adults (I3). The abstract does not clearly state use of reappraisal on pictures or report task activation results (I4 uncertain), so include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Abstract describes neural (whole-brain pattern) indices of spontaneous/implicit cognitive reappraisal during exposure to negative stimuli, indicating a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation in humans and reporting task-related brain activation findings. Thus inclusion criteria I1-I4 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

E1: This is a review paper without original human data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (no original emotion regulation/reappraisal task with participants), I3 (no healthy adult sample reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results from original data).

Abstract reports investigation of temporal brain activation during cognitive emotion regulation in bipolar disorder and schizophrenia, indicating an emotion regulation task. However, it does not specify use of reappraisal of pictures, whether task-based fMRI was used, or inclusion of a healthy control group. Insufficient information—include for full-text review.

This is a review article that synthesizes neuroimaging findings rather than reporting original human task-based fMRI data. Exclusion E1 applies. Inclusion criteria not met: not a task-based fMRI study (I1), does not report original emotion regulation/reappraisal task data (I2), does not include participants/groups (I3), and does not report original task-related activation results (I4).

Excluded because E2 is met (no healthy adult sample or control group reported). No inclusion criteria were met. Inclusion criteria not met: I1—this is resting-state fMRI, not task-based; I2—no emotion regulation/reappraisal task was used; I3—no healthy control group reported; I4—no task-related brain activation results reported.

This is a resting-state connectivity study assessing dispositional emotion regulation (ERQ) rather than a task-based reappraisal paradigm in which participants regulate their emotional responses to pictures. Inclusion met: I3 (includes healthy controls). Inclusion not met: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no in-scanner emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (no task-related activation reported). No exclusion criteria from the list are met.

E2 met: sample consists of adolescent girls (ages 9-16), so no healthy adult sample. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (explicit cognitive reappraisal regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (healthy adult group) is not satisfied.

Excluded: abstract describes an affect-labeling task in SAD patients without mention of a healthy control group. Meets exclusion E2 (no healthy adult sample). Inclusion I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related neural/connectivity results) are met. Does not meet I2 (task is affect labeling, not clearly reappraisal/emotion-regulation via reappraisal) and I3 (no healthy controls reported).

Abstract reports a task-based neuroimaging investigation of emotion regulation and reactivity in adult monozygotic twins, includes a low-risk (healthy) control group, and examines neural correlates (task-related brain activation). Therefore it appears to meet I1-I4 and no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

E1: This paper is a review/meta-analysis without original human task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an original task-based fMRI study), I2 (no original participants performing a reappraisal task), I3 (no original healthy adult sample reported), I4 (no original task-related activation results; only meta-analytic summaries).

No evidence the task involved explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal (I2 not met). Abstract describes an affective verbal working memory task with aversive/positive distractors, not instructions to increase/decrease one’s emotion. It reports task-based fMRI results (I1 and I4 met). Healthy adult sample not specified in abstract (I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria E1–E3 clearly apply.

Task-based fMRI study with healthy adult groups and reports task-related brain activation. The abstract does not state participants were explicitly instructed to regulate or reappraise their emotions (I2 not clearly met), so include for full-text review to confirm.

This is a resting-state fMRI study measuring spontaneous reappraisal (questionnaire) and DMN temporal dynamics; no task-based emotion regulation/reappraisal paradigm or task-evoked activation is reported. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (healthy adults). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing a reappraisal/emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (down-regulation of negative emotions) in N=20 healthy participants reporting task-related brain activation (prefrontal and amygdala). Meets I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

No explicit participant-instructed emotion regulation/reappraisal task described. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation or reappraisal task is not demonstrated; study used neuromodulation during an anger-induction game rather than instructing reappraisal of pictures).

Abstract indicates task-based fMRI measuring neural activity during explicit emotion regulation, so I1, I2, and I4 appear satisfied. The abstract does not specify use of reappraisal tactics, stimulus type (pictures), or participant health status, so full-text review is needed to confirm I3 and confirm reappraisal/picture details.

Excluded because E2: the study involves depressed adolescents and does not include a healthy adult sample. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (reappraisal/emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I3 (includes at least one healthy adult group).

Not a task-based fMRI study and does not report task-related brain activation (fails I1 and I4). Meets I2 (participants performed emotion reappraisal task) and I3 (healthy adult sample). No exclusion criteria clearly met.

E1 met: this is a meta-analysis (ALE) of published fMRI studies, not original empirical human data. While the paper synthesizes task-based fMRI reappraisal studies and reports ALE activation results, it is not a primary task-based fMRI study: I1 not met. I2-I4 are not demonstrated for original data in this article (no original participants or primary task activations reported).

EXCLUDED (E2): Task-based fMRI Cyberball study in adolescents (ages 11–17) with depressed and healthy youth. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal instruction; social exclusion paradigm), I3 (no healthy adult sample; participants are adolescents). Therefore excluded based on E2.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study that explicitly compared reappraisal (explicit emotion regulation) and free viewing of facial expressions and describes task-related brain activation. The sample's health status (healthy adults) is not explicitly stated in the abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm I3.

Study used resting-state fMRI and dispositional ERQ scores rather than a task-based emotion regulation/reappraisal task; no task-related activation reported. Inclusion met: I3 (healthy adults). Inclusion not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study reports white-matter network alterations in depersonalization/derealization disorder, not a task-based fMRI reappraisal study. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no evidence of task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I3 (no healthy control group reported), I4 (no task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria (E1–E3) are clearly met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal to up- and down-regulate positive emotion, with behavioral, zEMG, and blood-oxygen-level (neuroimaging) results. It meets I1, I2, and I4. The abstract does not explicitly state the sample are healthy adults (I3 unclear), so include for full-text review to confirm.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study examining effortful emotion regulation (reappraisal) and frontal-amygdala effective connectivity, indicating task-related brain results (I1, I2, I4). The abstract does not explicitly state inclusion of a healthy control group (I3 not demonstrated); therefore include for full-text review to confirm controls.

E1 met: this paper is a meta-analysis summarizing fMRI findings rather than reporting original task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a primary task-based fMRI study), I2 (no original participants performing reappraisal reported), I3 (no original healthy adult sample described), I4 (no original task-related activation results reported).

E2: Sample comprises adolescent girls (ages 16–17) and does not include a healthy adult group. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI assessing activation to sad faces), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (no evidence participants performed an explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I3 (no healthy adult sample).

This article is a narrative review/synthesis of prior functional neuroimaging studies rather than an original task-based fMRI study with human participants. Exclusion criteria met: E1. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical task-based fMRI study), I2 (no original reappraisal/emotion-regulation task performed), I3 (no participant groups reported), I4 (no original task-related activation results).

No evidence the study used reappraisal of pictures (I2 not met); abstract describes regulation of autobiographical memories and does not specify reappraisal nor use of pictured stimuli. Healthy control group not demonstrated (I3 not shown). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based neuroimaging implied) and I4 (reports brain activation/reactivity). No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) are clearly met.

Task-based fMRI study with human participants (primiparous mothers, N=26) performing an emotion-regulation task (distraction) and reporting task-related amygdala activation changes. Includes healthy adult participants. Although the strategy was distraction (not explicitly reappraisal) and stimuli were infant crying rather than pictures, the abstract meets the review's broad inclusion criteria for emotion-regulation fMRI studies, so include for full-text review.

No task-based fMRI: study used resting-state connectivity and trait measures of expressive suppression/reappraisal rather than a task in which participants regulated emotional responses to pictures. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (performed an ER/reappraisal task), I4 (reports task-related activation). I3 (healthy adult sample) is not demonstrated in the abstract. No exclusion criteria met.

Task-based fMRI with 60 healthy adult participants explicitly instructed to reappraise negative images to decrease emotional response; reports task-related neural activation results (PCA/discriminant analysis). Satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the study examined explicit/implicit emotional suppression, not reappraisal (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I2 (reappraisal) and I3 (healthy adults not explicitly stated). No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) apply.

Task-based fMRI with 49 healthy adult participants performing explicit cognitive reappraisal of aversive images (Reappraise vs Look-Negative), and reports whole-brain activation results; meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

E2: Study sample is adolescents; abstract gives no indication of any healthy adult participants. Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not explicitly stated), I2 (emotion regulation task implied but not clearly described as reappraisal), I4 (task-related activation results not reported in abstract). No inclusion criteria can be confirmed from abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study with explicit up-/down-regulation (reappraisal) of emotional responses to faces, includes a healthy control group, and reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract does not specify use of a task-based fMRI reappraisal paradigm, nor whether healthy adult controls were included or that task-related activation results are reported. Insufficient information to determine inclusion based on abstract alone; include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (includes healthy adult participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; used resting-state functional connectivity), I2 (participants did not perform an emotion regulation/reappraisal task; study assessed habitual reappraisal), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Task-based fMRI study where participants used distancing (a reappraisal tactic) to down-regulate emotion to pictures; includes a healthy control group and reports task-related neural activation results (ventral striatum regulation score and task contrasts). Satisfies I1–I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because E2: the abstract describes a sample of women with BPD and does not indicate a healthy control group. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI study) and I4 (reports neural/task-related activation). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (task is provocation-focused rumination, not clearly an instructed reappraisal/emotion-regulation task) and I3 (no healthy adult sample reported).

Excluded because the study is not a task-based fMRI investigation and does not involve an emotion regulation/reappraisal task nor report task-related activation results. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (healthy adults). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Abstract explicitly investigates emotion regulation and associated brain activation/connectivity, but does not specify the imaging modality (fMRI) nor whether a healthy adult control group was included. Insufficient information to confirm I1 and I3, so include for full-text review.

EXCLUDED because the study used an emotional face processing task without instructions to regulate/ reappraise emotional responses (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related activation). No exclusion criteria met (none of E1–E3 apply).

E2: No healthy adult sample — control group is age-matched adolescents. Meets I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (reappraisal/detachment emotion regulation task), and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Does not meet I3 (includes at least one healthy adult group).

Excluded because the study used resting-state fMRI after an anger induction rather than a task-based reappraisal/regulation paradigm. No evidence participants performed reappraisal or other explicit regulation (I2 not met), it is not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met), and it does not report task-related activation results (I4 not met). Inclusion criterion I3 (healthy adult sample) is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract mentions changes in brain function across emotional reactivity and regulation paradigms but does not specify task-based fMRI, use of reappraisal on pictures, or inclusion of a healthy control group. Insufficient information to confirm inclusion criteria; include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (includes healthy control group). Inclusion criteria not met / not demonstrated: I2 (abstract does not indicate participants performed an emotion regulation/reappraisal task), I1 (abstract does not clearly state a task-based fMRI paradigm), I4 (task-related brain activation results are not explicitly reported).

Task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants performing cognitive reappraisal of negative/neutral pictures; reports behavioral and task-related neural activation results (PFC, amygdala). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria evident from abstract.

Abstract reports a structural neuroimaging study of resilience in police officers, not a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation. No mention of an emotion reappraisal task or task-related activation results. Thus I1 and I4 are not met; I2 and I3 are not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria clearly met.

Excluded under E1 (meta-analysis/review without original primary human fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (includes healthy control groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results via meta-analysis). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a primary task-based fMRI study), I2 (does not report original participants performing reappraisal tasks itself).

Task-based fMRI study with 27 healthy adult females using cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) and distraction while viewing aversive/neutral pictures; reports BOLD/task-related brain activation and subjective reports. Meets I1-I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

Excluded due to E2: sample consists of adolescent girls only (no healthy adult group). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation/connectivity). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no healthy adult sample).

No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) are met. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (abstract does not describe a task-based fMRI study or any fMRI methods), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation results), I2 (no evidence participants performed an explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal task; discusses natural responses to stress), I3 (participant health status/groups not specified).

Excluding because the abstract does not describe an emotion regulation/reappraisal task or a task-based fMRI study of reappraisal. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (healthy control group present), I4 (reports fMRI neural responses). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not clearly a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation), I2 (no evidence participants performed reappraisal/emotion regulation on pictures).

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of affect labeling (an emotion-regulation strategy) and presents task-related neural activation results predicting outcomes. However it does not specify use of reappraisal strategies, picture stimuli, or whether a healthy adult sample was tested. Insufficient details to confirm all eligibility, so include for full-text review.

Abstract explicitly examines emotional reactivity and regulation in GAD, indicating an emotion regulation task was used, but it does not specify the use of reappraisal, task-based fMRI, or inclusion of healthy control participants. Insufficient information to determine eligibility; include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal paradigm, reports task-related brain activation, and includes a healthy control group (nonusing controls). No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Excluded because the sample consists of 'girls' (minors) and the abstract does not indicate inclusion of a healthy adult sample, so E2 is met. The abstract does describe a task-based fMRI study of reappraisal and reports neural activation (I1, I2, I4 are satisfied), but I3 (includes at least one group of healthy adults) is not met or demonstrated.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal (distancing) in human participants (ages 6–23), reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results (amygdala, vmPFC, vlPFC), and includes healthy participants including adults. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract addresses emotion regulation and brain function in anxiety and depression but provides insufficient details to confirm a task-based fMRI reappraisal paradigm, presence of a healthy control group, or task-related activation results. No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Recommend full-text review to determine I1–I4.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a cognitive reappraisal paradigm in non-medicated depressed youth and healthy controls, with reported task-related brain activation results (amygdala, vmPFC, dorsal midline). It therefore meets I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study with an explicit emotion regulation instruction (distraction) during anger provocation, includes a healthy non-offender control group, and reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports comparisons between gambling disorder patients and healthy controls on self-report and brain activation measures of emotion regulation but does not specify task-based fMRI, use of reappraisal, or regulation of responses to pictures; insufficient information to determine I1, I2, and I4 from abstract, so include for full-text review.

Task-based fMRI study using an explicit reappraisal task with IAPS pictures (reinterpretation), reports task-related brain activations (amygdala, insula, temporal, parahippocampal regions), and appears to involve healthy adult participants (non-clinical trait study). Meets all inclusion criteria; no exclusion criteria identified from abstract.

E2 met: study includes only a GAD patient sample (no healthy control group). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performed emotion regulation strategies: acceptance, suppression, worry), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I3 (no healthy adult sample reported).

Excluded under E1 (systematic review without original human data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an original task-based fMRI study), I2 (no participants performing a reappraisal task reported), I3 (no original healthy control group), I4 (no task-related activation results).

Abstract indicates a task-based fMRI study measuring ACC and amygdala activation during emotion regulation to predict CBT response in SAD, fulfilling I1, I2, and I4. The abstract does not specify whether a healthy control group was included (I3 unclear). No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Include for full-text review to determine presence of healthy adult sample and extract task details.

Task-based fMRI study that examines implicit reappraisal of unpleasant pictures and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity. It investigates reappraisal (albeit implicit), and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text needed to confirm participant health status and explicitness of regulation instructions.

E2 met: abstract reports 34 patients with SAD but no healthy control group. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (reappraisal emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I3 (includes at least one healthy adult group) is not met.

Task-based fMRI with human adults reporting task-related brain activations. Participants performed implicit emotion regulation (attention shift away and reflective appraisal of their own emotional responses) to emotional pictures; although regulation was implicit rather than explicit reappraisal, the review's I2 accepts broad emotion regulation/reappraisal paradigms. Include for full-text review to confirm specifics of reappraisal instructions and sample.

Explicit task-based fMRI study (N=82) using an explicit emotion regulation/reappraisal task; reports task-related brain activation results and includes healthy adult participants. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using reappraisal (down-/up-regulation) and reports task-related effective connectivity/activation linked to regulation success. Participant health status not specified in abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm presence of healthy adult sample.

Task-based fMRI study where participants attended to, suppressed, or cognitively reappraised negative images, explicitly using reappraisal (meets I1 and I2). Sample includes 47 healthy adult females (I3). Reports task-related brain activation and PPI results (I4). No exclusion criteria met based on the abstract.

Abstract does not specify that participants performed an emotion regulation/reappraisal task or that task-based fMRI was used, nor does it clearly state inclusion of a healthy adult sample. Information is insufficient to determine eligibility, so include for full-text review to assess I1–I4.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study that used cognitive emotion regulation (CER) during aversive Pavlovian conditioning and reports task-related brain activation changes. It is unclear whether stimuli were pictures and the abstract does not explicitly state the sample was healthy adults, so full-text review is needed to confirm I3 and the picture-specific objective.

Task-based fMRI study using an explicit emotion reappraisal paradigm in human participants with low and high externalizing psychopathology (includes healthy/low-EXT group). Abstract reports task-related neural activation differences (amygdala, parietal, occipital). Fits all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

EXCLUDED because the task used distraction (attentional deployment) rather than reappraisal. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (includes healthy adults), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (does not involve reappraisal; participants performed distraction). No exclusion criteria (E1–E3) apply.

Abstract describes a task-based neuroimaging study of positive reappraisal (reinterpreting negative stimuli) and reports task-related activations in ventral striatum, vmPFC, and amygdala. It meets I1, I2, and I4. The abstract does not explicitly state the sample are healthy adults (I3 not clearly reported), so include for full-text review to confirm participant characteristics.

Task-based fMRI study that explicitly used cognitive emotion regulation in the form of reappraisal and reports task-related brain activation (left DLPFC and connectivity) (I1, I2, I4). The abstract does not specify whether a healthy control group was included (I3 unclear). Include for full-text review to confirm presence of healthy adults.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 — the study examined spontaneous/primed expressive suppression, not participants actively using reappraisal to regulate emotional responses to pictures. The review objective targets reappraisal studies, so exclude.

All inclusion criteria (I1,I2,I3,I4) are met, but the study does not address the review objective: emotion regulation was elicited with odours, not pictures. No exclusion criteria (E1-E3) apply. Excluded because stimulus modality (not pictures) makes it ineligible for this review focused on regulation of responses to pictures.

Abstract mentions neural basis of emotion regulation but provides no methodological details (no explicit mention of task-based fMRI, reappraisal of pictures, participant sample, or reported task-related activations). Insufficient information to determine eligibility from abstract alone; include for full-text review.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) in combat-exposed veterans with and without PTSD, includes a non-PTSD control group, and discusses brain activation (prefrontal cortex, amygdala) during regulation. This matches inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met in the abstract.
